name: TPH2900ENH_L1Q_M
title: 200 V, 33 A N-channel U-MOSVIII-H power MOSFET in SOP Advance
summary: A single N-channel enhancement MOSFET from Toshiba's U-MOSVIII-H silicon line, packed in the eight-lead SOP Advance flat package (5 × 6 mm footprint, 0.95 mm tall) with an exposed pad on its underside. It blocks 200 V, carries 33 A continuously (36 A silicon limit) and 102 A in 1 ms pulses, and dissipates 78 W with the case held at 25 °C. With 10 V on the gate the on-resistance is 24 mΩ typical, 29 mΩ max; total gate charge is 22 nC and switching charge 8.2 nC. Aimed at high-efficiency DC-DC converters and switching regulators.

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: Resistive-load switching fixture for tr, ton, tf and toff. A 0 V/10 V gate pulse, 10 µs wide at no more than 1 % duty, drives the gate directly; a 4.7 Ω resistor RG runs from the gate node to ground. The source is grounded. A 6.06 Ω load RL links the drain to a supply of about 100 V, the drain current is 16.5 A, and the output voltage is taken at the drain.

parts.value: VGS pulse, 0 V/10 V, tw = 10 µs, duty ≤ 1 %

operation.text: Offered for high-efficiency DC-DC converters and switching voltage regulators, with fast switching, low gate charge, low on-resistance and at most 10 µA of leakage at 200 V as its selling points.

Enhancement mode: the threshold lies between 2.0 V and 4.0 V at VDS = 10 V and 1.0 mA, and the gate is rated ±20 V. On-resistance is specified at 10 V drive only (24 mΩ typ, 29 mΩ max at 16.5 A). In the transfer curves at VDS = 10 V the channel starts to conduct near 3.3 V at 100 °C, 3.6 V at 25 °C and 3.9 V at -55 °C, and passes 30 A by about 5 V. The threshold falls with temperature, from about 3.4 V at -55 °C to about 2.05 V at 150 °C. Gate resistance is 4.0 Ω typ, 6.0 Ω max.

At 10 V gate drive and 25 °C the on-resistance stays close to 24 mΩ up to roughly 20 A, then climbs to about 40 mΩ at 108 A. It rises with temperature from about 12 mΩ at -55 °C through about 19.5 mΩ at 0 °C to about 61 mΩ at 150 °C for 8.3 A and 16.5 A, and about 65 mΩ at 33 A.
The drain-source breakdown is at least 200 V with the gate at 0 V, but only 140 V minimum with the gate held at -20 V (V(BR)DSX, ID = 10 mA).

At VDD ≈ 100 V, ID = 33 A and VGS = 10 V the gate takes 22 nC in total, of which 9.0 nC brings it to the plateau (Qgs1), 4.4 nC is the Miller charge (Qgd) and 8.2 nC is the switching charge QSW. In the gate-charge curves the plateau sits near 5.9 V; at VDD ≈ 40 V the gate leaves the plateau at about 12 nC and reaches 10 V at about 21 nC, at 100 V and 160 V about 22 nC. Resistive switching at 100 V and 16.5 A gives 8.0 ns rise, 20 ns turn-on, 12 ns fall and 36 ns turn-off, typical.

With VDS = 100 V and the gate shorted, Ciss is 1700 pF typ (2200 pF max), Coss 180 pF typ and Crss 7.0 pF typ (50 pF max). Coss and Crss fall steeply between about 18 V and 30 V: Coss from around 1.5 nF to under 400 pF and Crss from around 65 pF to under 10 pF. Ciss stays between about 1.7 nF and 1.9 nF across the range.

The source-to-drain diode carries 102 A in pulses (channel kept at or below 150 °C) and drops at most 1.2 V at 33 A with the gate at 0 V. Reverse current at a given drain voltage grows with gate drive: at VDS = -0.4 V the curve for VGS = 10 V shows about 15 A, the curve for VGS = 0 V less than 1 A.
Rated for 176 mJ in a single avalanche pulse and 33 A avalanche current, tested from VDD = 60 V into 250 µH starting at Tch = 25 °C.

Channel-to-case resistance is 1.60 °C/W max, so 78 W is allowed with the case at 25 °C, falling in a straight line from 25 °C to zero at 150 °C. On the 25.4 mm square, 0.8 mm FR-4 test boards the 10 s figures are 44.6 °C/W and 2.8 W on board (a), which carries a large copper area, and 78.1 °C/W and 1.6 W on board (b), which carries only small pads; both power figures hold flat to 25 °C ambient and fall linearly to zero at 150 °C. The transient thermal impedance curves start at about 0.05 °C/W at 100 µs; the case-referred curve settles at about 1.6 °C/W after a few seconds, while the board curves reach about 84 °C/W (board a) and 177 °C/W (board b) in steady state.

The safe operating area is drawn for single pulses at Ta = 25 °C (10 µs, 100 µs, 1 ms, 10 ms) and for DC at Tc = 25 °C, bounded by the pulsed and continuous drain current limits, an RDS(ON) line at low voltage and VDSS = 200 V. All of these curves shrink linearly as temperature rises.

The part can be damaged by electrostatic discharge and needs ESD-safe handling. The top face carries the part number on two lines, TPH290 over 0ENH (or a shortened code), a lot number, and a round mark in the pin 1 corner.

The characteristic curves are reference data and are not production tested unless a curve says otherwise; the power derating, transient thermal impedance and safe operating area curves are guaranteed maximums.
